summary.text: Bale Dalton is the Democratic nominee for the open Florida 7th Congressional District seat. A U.S. Naval Academy graduate and Navy helicopter pilot with over 24 years in the Navy and Navy Reserve, he later worked for Sen. Bill Nelson and served as NASA Chief of Staff. He won the August 18 Democratic primary with 45.6% of the vote and, per his candidate survey, is campaigning on costs such as gas, health care premiums, housing and property insurance.

paragraphs.text: Dalton says he was born and raised in Central Florida and has spent his career in public service. He graduated from the U.S. Naval Academy and served over 24 years in the Navy and Navy Reserve, including 13 years of active duty as a helicopter pilot, deploying to Iraq, Afghanistan, the Horn of Africa, and the Pacific.

As a Navy helicopter pilot, he says, he flew search and rescue flights after Hurricane Katrina, medical evacuation missions in Kuwait, and special operations missions in Iraq and Africa, and directed combat air support with Navy SEALs in Afghanistan.

Dalton worked for Sen. Bill Nelson helping Florida veterans access care and benefits, then returned to active duty as commanding officer of a Navy special-operations support helicopter squadron. He later worked at an aerospace company, where he says he used his military background to improve efficiency and operations, and served as NASA Chief of Staff, managing 16,500 employees.
On August 18, 2026, he won the Democratic primary with 45.6% of the vote, ahead of Marialana Kinter and Alan Grayson.
